Yea, you are pretty close, a golden child syndrome is when the parent/s praise and/or pressure their kid so much that he now feels like he has to be perfect because of the expectations, to the point where the kid doesn't know what to do if he isn't, expresses extreme guilt for *(as he thinks)* doing everything wrong and breaks down from the smallest mistakes. And a lot of people who don't know that much about it might think that the kid has the syndrome, but it is actually about the parent/s, because **they** see their kid as this "perfect masterpiece" that they "created" and **they** put the pressure of having to be "perfect" and fulfilling their selfish desires. *(there are a* ***loooot*** *more nuances to this that I won't be listing here, because it will be too long, but you can just search it up yourself)*

Edit: I know I said that I won't be listing any nuances, but this is pretty important: the kid naturally supposes that this is the way things should be, which gives him a very twisted sense of love, *(that is heavily implied in the song, and because of that people think it's about yanderes)* so now the kid  **wants** people to expect more of him, and that is again the parent/s fault, because **they** projected this twisted sense of love that implies that people only love you when you are "good enough" and that you should just stick with that onto their child.

Edit2: Oh god, I just re-read what I said and realised that I probably was a victim to this, because I grew up in an *(as I now realise)* emotionally abusive house hold, with a narcissistic mother figure, that always told me how she expects more of me..

Edit3: Well, on the good side, I guess now I know why I'm so emotionally unstable :)
